newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan receives first China application for links.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan receives first China application for links.

text.p: A China shipping company has applied to rival Taiwan's port authorities for the first direct sailing of the Taiwan strait since 1949, Taiwan newspapers reported on Friday.

Fujian Foreign Trade Centre Shipping Co, one of the five state-run shippers that received approval on Wednesday from China's communist government to make cross-straits passages, has submitted its application to port authorities in southern Kaohsiung, local newspapers said.
The mainland shipper applied to sail between Kaohsiung and mainland's coastal city of Fuzhou, they said.
Taiwan's transport ministry is expected to review the application on Monday.
Friday was a public holiday and officials could not be reached for comment.
Taiwan's transportation ministry said on Thursday it expected to receive applications from the five newly authorised China firms within a few days and would approve them swiftly.
"The ministry will be able to process the mainland shippers for cross-strait links in less than a week after receiving them," transport vice minister Mao Chi-kuo told reporters.

Ting Chan-neng, head of the ministry's navigation and aviation section, said direct crossings could begin as soon as 10 days from Thursday if, as expected, the mainland firms' paperwork is received within two or three days.

Taiwan has banned all direct contacts with China since 1949, when it was split from the newly communist mainland by a civil war. Cross-strait trade and investment nonetheless has flowered since a political thaw began in the late 1980s, most of it routed "indirectly" via Hong Kong.
The booming economic unofficial ties have created huge pressure for an easing of the shipping ban.
